response.consequence: Slots that start inside working hours but end after them are treated as available and offered to invitees, so bookings can run past the organizer's working hours.
response.explanation: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `end` is computed with the same expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`). The `end > workingHour.endTime` test therefore never uses the slot's end time. It should use `slotEndTime`. Take working hours of 09:00–17:00 and a 60-minute event. A slot starting at 16:30 has start=990, which is not below the 540 start and not above the 1020 end, so it counts as inside working hours. It actually ends at 17:30. A related defect is at line 114. It compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which compares references and is always false, so the zero-length-override branch never fires.

other_findings.consequence: A zero-length date override (blocked day) may not block slots as intended.
other_findings.explanation: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The branch meant to reject an override whose start equals its end (a day off) never runs. For such an override, a slot only falls through to the later start/end checks.
other_findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === in date override check
